Ok I think I figured it out. Branch with fixes: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commits/fix-int-tests/

Three different issues, involving different remotes. (Btw, all 3 tests are new ones I added -- not regressions.)

### TestFixCase

Proposed fix: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/a369fcb9059c7bd5e672f8a7c9d9d28b4bf7c3aa
I think this actually revealed a pre-existing bug in rclone that was not previously covered by the tests. In a nutshell, `operations.moveOrCopyFile` had a special section to handle changing case of a file on a case insensitive remote, but `operations.Move` did not. The issue only affects backends that are incapable of renaming a file in-place to an equal-folding name, which is not all case-insensitive remotes. This is why I did not catch it when testing on macOS (which is case-insensitive but can rename in place.)

Note also that while testing, Dropbox sometimes complained about `too_many_write_operations` unless I slept for a second or two between moves (https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/a85313cee4d22a097768c4a7e0de380abd3c9938). This probably isn't the right fix, and may not actually be needed (is it just a limitation of the free account I'm using? does the real integration test account have higher API limits?)

### TestCaseInsensitiveMoveFileDryRun
https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/a2dccf8ba35f2c9ccc31d67cbc531dd79f69f3b6

It appears that `ci.DryRun = true` affects the behavior of `r.WriteObject` on `chunker` only, and no other remotes. This change puts a quick bandaid on it by setting it later on in the test, but perhaps the underlying issue warrants a closer look at some point... is `chunker` checking `ci.DryRun` itself in a way that no other remote does? If so, should it? (Does this break encapsulation?)

### TestApplyTransforms

I think this one is actually an issue with the 3 failing backends (Jottacloud, Koofr, and Owncloud) not the test or code. I suspect the issue is that these 3 are normalizing to NFC on the server side, so they are actually incapable of supporting `NoUnicodeNormalization` (i.e. if you give it NFD, it will convert it to NFC anyway). A quick search seems to confirm this (for example, see Owncloud issue 6338.) So, not sure what the right fix is here -- perhaps we should just skip this test for these 3 backends, by name?

CI is passing for my branch with the fixes: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/actions/runs/7632382555

Dropbox is stingy with there iops and a lot of rclone users run with `--tpslimit 12` which seems to be the right number for uploading lots of files - not sure about moves.

> ### TestApplyTransforms
> I think this one is actually an issue with the 3 failing backends (Jottacloud, Koofr, and Owncloud) not the test or code. I suspect the issue is that these 3 are normalizing to NFC on the server side, so they are actually incapable of supporting `NoUnicodeNormalization` (i.e. if you give it NFD, it will convert it to NFC anyway). A quick search seems to confirm this (for example, see Owncloud issue 6338.) So, not sure what the right fix is here -- perhaps we should just skip this test for these 3 backends, by name?

I prefer not to have backends named in the tests.

This can be done in two ways
1. one is add an exception to [the integration test config](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/master/fstest/test_all/config.yaml) - the test will still fail but the integration tests will pass as this is an allowed failure.
2. Add a Feature flag to the backend so we know which backends can't support `NoUnicodeNormalization`.

I don't think the Feature flag is useful except in the tests, so I'd probably go with 1. What do you think?

> CI is passing for my branch with the fixes: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/actions/runs/7632382555

Thanks for fixing those @nielash . I pulled those locally gave them a test and I've merged them now and we can check [the integration tests](https://pub.rclone.org/integration-tests/current/) tomorrow to see how we did!

> I don't think the Feature flag is useful except in the tests, so I'd probably go with 1. What do you think?

I agree. I also have one other idea, inspired by [this test](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/master/vfs/vfs_case_test.go#L49-L64) which I happened to be looking at yesterday. The test ultimately tests case sensitivity but first tests whether the test can even be performed, and skips if not. We could potentially do the same here, without needing the backend to self-report its features (which could eventually change).

On the other hand, it's sort of a self-fulfilling prophecy... and if a backend were to change its encoding some day, maybe that's a change we'd want to know about?

> We could potentially do the same here, without needing the backend to self-report its features

Here's an example of how this could be done here: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/da487ba695d85af4751f799702f9b8e4fcf50bdc

@ncw I see that `TestFixCase` is now failing in a different way, and I think I see why -- the `dirCache` is not getting properly flushed after the first move. This fixes it for me on OneDrive: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/commit/365f5394c674506710266a9a084541d5876fcf27 (although I wonder if it would be more properly addressed in `dircache`... is this expected behavior?)

I think this should fix it for most of the others too, as they are failing in the same way and also use `dircache`. Possible exceptions are `Linkbox` and `jottacloud`, which I think may be failing due to [this](https://rclone.org/jottacloud/#troubleshooting):

> Jottacloud exhibits some inconsistent behaviours regarding deleted files and folders which may cause Copy, Move and DirMove operations to previously deleted paths to fail. Emptying the trash should help in such cases.

Looking at the others now.

> > We could potentially do the same here, without needing the backend to self-report its features
> 
> Here's an example of how this could be done here: [nielash@da487ba](https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/da487ba695d85af4751f799702f9b8e4fcf50bdc)

I think that looks fine :-) Do you want to PR it? Or I can cherry-pick it to master if you want.

> @ncw I see that `TestFixCase` is now failing in a different way, and I think I see why -- the `dirCache` is not getting properly flushed after the first move. This fixes it for me on OneDrive: [365f539](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/commit/365f5394c674506710266a9a084541d5876fcf27) (although I wonder if it would be more properly addressed in `dircache`... is this expected behavior?)

I don't understand why that fix changes the directory cache? If we are making a new backend it should have its own directory cache. /insert puzzled face emoji

Comments on that bit of code:
- `fs.NewFs` is expensive - some backends do multiple HTTP calls when you make them - can we avoid it?
- The `filepath.Join` look wrong - rclone paths are always unix paths so this should be `path.Join` or possibly even `fspath.Join`

What change would you propose in the directory cache code to fix it?

> I think this should fix it for most of the others too, as they are failing in the same way and also use `dircache`. Possible exceptions are `Linkbox` and `jottacloud`, which I think may be failing due to [this](https://rclone.org/jottacloud/#troubleshooting):
> 
> > Jottacloud exhibits some inconsistent behaviours regarding deleted files and folders which may cause Copy, Move and DirMove operations to previously deleted paths to fail. Emptying the trash should help in such cases.
> 
> Looking at the others now.

:+1:

> I don't understand why that fix changes the directory cache?

The `DirMove` method calls `f.dirCache.DirMove` to set up the move:

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/2abeda5961615c304348c4886a1d42f4ae30c876/backend/onedrive/onedrive.go#L1717

and then flushes the cache after the move:

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/2abeda5961615c304348c4886a1d42f4ae30c876/backend/onedrive/onedrive.go#L1762

We do two moves [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/365f5394c674506710266a9a084541d5876fcf27/fs/sync/sync.go#L1161-L1167) (to temp name, then real name). The first move succeeds. For the second move, `f.dirCache.DirMove` returns `fs.ErrorDirExists` instead of `nil` because it thinks the old dir is still there. The reason it thinks that is because `newDirFs` was created before the move that flushed the cache, and `newDirFs` wasn't involved in that first move, so its cache wasn't flushed. So when we use it for the second move, it still has the old cache. But if we create it after the first move, then it inherits the correct already-flushed cache. 

It's possible I'm misunderstanding something, but that really seems to be what's happening as far as I can tell!

> * `fs.NewFs` is expensive - some backends do multiple HTTP calls when you make them - can we avoid it?

Possibly -- the issue is that `sync.MoveDir` doesn't take a `remote` string, it expects the root. But maybe I can find a different function to use. 

Would `cache.Get` be a better choice?

> * The `filepath.Join` look wrong - rclone paths are always unix paths so this should be `path.Join` or possibly even `fspath.Join`

That's actually what I had originally, but then it [errored on windows](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/7356#issuecomment-1758700673) because of the `\`.

> What change would you propose in the directory cache code to fix it?

I'm not quite sure yet. This may just be expected behavior, but I think the thing that is surprising to me is that the caller would need to be concerned with tracking which Fs's have been flushed and when... I'd have expected the backend to manage that independently, so that the outcome doesn't change depending on where in your code you call `NewFs`. I guess I assumed I had a pointer to some shared cache, instead of a copy.

### TestApplyTransforms

Yes, I think we should go ahead with https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/da487ba695d85af4751f799702f9b8e4fcf50bdc. I tested it with Dropbox just now and confirmed this is the issue:

```
    check_test.go:575: Fs is incapable of running test, skipping: NFC checkfile vs. NFD remote (expected: 測試_Русский___ě_áñ (NFD) actual: 測試_Русский___ě_áñ (NFC))
```

I guess a surprising number of backends auto-convert NFD to NFC (it turns out to be more than three -- we were previously skipping all the ones without `MD5` support).

It looks like `mailru` might still fail even with this fix, as it won't even attempt to convert it to something it finds valid:

```
run.go:285: Failed to put "測試_Русский___ě_áñ" to "[rclone-test-kajugal2ciruquc7hihifuy6]": invalid characters in object name
```

So that one may need another look. But I think this should resolve the others.

### TestCaseInsensitiveMoveFileDryRun

This one appears to be fixed now.

### TestFixCase

The two outliers here are `jottacloud` and `linkbox`. `jottacloud` has a relavant [known issue](https://rclone.org/jottacloud/#troubleshooting) and is failing before it even gets to the real test. It appears to be not only case-insensitive but also not even case-preserving (we're putting `EXISTING` and it is returning `existing`.) So, I don't think it is actually capable of supporting `--fix-case`, and it probably needs either an exception or to be skipped with a meta-test similar to https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/da487ba695d85af4751f799702f9b8e4fcf50bdc.

`linkbox` seems to be failing all kinds of encoding tests at the moment:

```
TestIntegration/FsMkdir/FsEncoding/leading_dot, TestIntegration/FsMkdir/FsEncoding/trailing_space, TestIntegration/FsMkdir/FsEncoding/trailing_CR, TestIntegration/FsMkdir/FsEncoding/trailing_LF, TestIntegration/FsMkdir/FsEncoding/trailing_HT, … (10 more)
```

so it is maybe not surprising that it's failing this one too. Seems like there is some larger issue there.

The others are all failing in the same specific way as `onedrive`, so I predict they would be fixed by https://github.com/rclone/rclone/commit/365f5394c674506710266a9a084541d5876fcf27, although it remains entirely possible that I'm misunderstanding _why_ the change fixes it (in which case, please correct me 😄)

> Possibly -- the issue is that `sync.MoveDir` doesn't take a `remote` string, it expects the root. But maybe I can find a different function to use.

Maybe [`operations.DirMove`](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/2abeda5961615c304348c4886a1d42f4ae30c876/fs/operations/operations.go#L2206) is the answer? Could it be that simple?

@ncw I tried `operations.DirMove` and it worked like a charm. Seems like a cleaner solution for multiple issues here. Thoughts? https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/34c632e51d568d865e515a7efba6a9504466b516

> @ncw I tried `operations.DirMove` and it worked like a charm. Seems like a cleaner solution for multiple issues here. Thoughts? [nielash@34c632e](https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/34c632e51d568d865e515a7efba6a9504466b516)

Yes DirMove seems like a good idea. That was made for the vfs to rename directories and will use the underlying `DirMove` primitives if available so will be much more efficient.

> It's possible I'm misunderstanding something, but that really seems to be what's happening as far as I can tell!

Got it - your explanation sounds correct to me.

Will reply to other queries above later!
